minutes.headline: Committee approved the high school's move to a one-year US history course with new half-year electives.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a history department proposal to replace the two-year US history sequence with a one-year course plus focused electives, and approved it. It held a first reading of the harassment and search-and-seizure policies, and sent the school bus bid out. It also got the superintendent's FY20 budget update and a review of the foundation budget forums, and gave feedback on the TC Passios options.

public_comment.topic: A resident from 56 Wedding Street supported TCP option one but raised possible traffic impact from a road near the back wing.

what_happened.line: The School Committee accepted the history department's new social studies pathway, replacing the two-year US history sequence with a one-year course plus electives.
The committee voted to send the school bus transportation bid out as presented, as a three-year contract with single-year options.
The committee told the town manager it prefers TCP option one for the future plan.
Policy 542 returns as a first reading with changes, and policy 546 goes to the attorney with questions, both due at the next meeting.
The committee accepted donations to Turkey Hill Elementary.

why_it_matters: The history change alters what high school students take in US history, and the bus bid sets the term of a school transportation contract that is paid for from the school budget, mostly taxes.

The town manager's FY20 guideline is a percentage increase, and a level service school budget would come in higher, so the gap between the two may shape the budget residents are later asked to vote on.
watch_next: Policies 542 and 546 return at the next School Committee meeting.
The transportation bid is due in February.
